title: Tăng trưởng và tài nguyên · Discuss both views
prompt: Some people support requiring governments to limit material consumption even if economic growth slows, while others oppose it because of the risks it could create. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.

Máy giặt sửa được minh họa giảm nhu cầu vật liệu từ gốc, khác với xử lý sau khi thành rác. Giảm doanh số đột ngột làm lao động chịu chi phí chuyển đổi. Hỗ trợ chuyển nghề và phân biệt nhu cầu thiết yếu với thay mới tránh dùng mục tiêu môi trường để bỏ qua phân phối tổn thất.

paragraphs: Supporters argue that lower material use can reduce environmental pressure beyond what recycling achieves. Opponents respond that abrupt restrictions can threaten employment in industries that depend on high sales volumes. I favour reducing wasteful material consumption, but opponents rightly insist that workers and households meeting essential needs should not bear the same adjustment burden as discretionary replacement spending.

Lower material use can reduce environmental pressure beyond what recycling achieves. Longer product lifetimes reduce the need for extraction, manufacturing and repeated transport. A repairable washing machine can provide years of additional service without another manufacturing cycle. The objective is to provide the same useful service with fewer replacement cycles, rather than simply count a larger volume of material entering recycling bins. Keeping a washing machine in service reduces replacement demand, whereas denying a first essential appliance to a low-income household raises a different question of fairness.

Abrupt restrictions can threaten employment in industries that depend on high sales volumes. Firms built around frequent replacement purchases may respond to falling demand by cutting employment before workers can move elsewhere. An environmental gain can therefore create concentrated local losses, especially where the same industry supports many neighbouring businesses. Transition plans should support workers and distinguish essential consumption from avoidable waste. Worker support should connect declining activities with viable new roles, while exemptions for essential needs prevent a uniform consumption target from worsening deprivation. Progress should be measured by material use per useful service and by workers' transition prospects, rather than by lower sales figures alone.

Environmental protection provides the stronger reason to move beyond replacement-led growth, while employment concerns require a fair transition; longer product use is persuasive when essential needs and affected workers remain protected.

paragraphs.quote: Abrupt restrictions can threaten employment in industries that depend on high sales volumes. Firms built around frequent replacement purchases may respond to falling demand by cutting employment before workers can move elsewhere. An environmental gain can therefore create concentrated local losses, especially where the same industry supports many neighbouring businesses. Transition plans should support workers and distinguish essential consumption from avoidable waste. Worker support should connect declining activities with viable new roles, while exemptions for essential needs prevent a uniform consumption target from worsening deprivation. Progress should be measured by material use per useful service and by workers' transition prospects, rather than by lower sales figures alone.
